Triggers.value: The same time of day the event occurred

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Being in circumstances that remind me of the event (eg, being in the dark).
Dates or anniversaries connected to the event
I spend money impulsively to distract or comfort myself

Memory.value: There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try
The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me
I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.

Negative Appraisals.value: My reactions since the event show that I am a lousy coper
My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy

vignette: Lena, a 66-year-old shopowner of Oceania ethnicity, has been living with the haunting memories of an encounter with police violence that occurred several years ago. The event itself was traumatic and deeply unsettling, leaving her with enduring emotional scars. The incident took place late in the evening when Lena’s shop was burglarized. As she called for help, a group of officers arrived but misinterpreted her distress signals as aggressive behavior. In the ensuing confrontation, Lena was forcefully restrained and intimidated by one officer who held his weapon close to her face, causing extreme fear and disorientation. This experience left her feeling watched and vulnerable, particularly during the late evening hours when the event occurred. Since then, whenever it is around that same time of day, Lena experiences intense feelings of being observed and becomes dizzy or lightheaded. These triggers have led her to avoid dark places and circumstances reminiscent of that fateful night, such as being alone in her shop after dusk. This avoidance has extended to anniversaries related to the event, where she finds herself spending more time in compulsive shopping sprees to distract from these overwhelming feelings. Lena struggles with memory gaps regarding parts of the traumatic event; no matter how hard she tries, certain moments remain a blur. The intensity and extremity of her experience make it feel unreal, and she often cannot put the frightening events into words. These memory issues have compounded her fears and inadequacies, reinforcing her belief that she is inadequate and unable to cope effectively with stress. Her tendency to avoid circumstances that remind her of the event has led to a pattern where she compulsively spends money as a means to distract herself from these memories and feelings. However, this behavior only serves to further erode her sense of self-worth, feeding into her negative appraisals such as feeling like a bad copier and fearing she is going crazy. Lena's memory issues are intertwined with her maladaptive strategies; the more she tries to avoid or distract herself from painful memories, the harder it becomes for her to recall details of what actually happened. This lack of clarity exacerbates her fears and inadequacies, creating a vicious cycle where each component reinforces the other. For example, when Lena experiences dizziness around 8 PM, the time of day the incident occurred, she immediately feels like she is being watched again. These triggers lead to her spending compulsively to distract herself from these feelings. However, the more she spends and avoids dealing with her trauma directly, the less clear her memories become, which in turn reinforces her negative appraisals about her own inadequacy and inability to cope. These patterns have taken a toll on her daily life as a shopowner. She finds it increasingly difficult to manage her store after dark and often leaves early or closes earlier than necessary. This has led to financial strains and strained relationships with regular customers who expect the shop to be open during its usual hours. The cumulative effect of these symptoms finally prompted Lena to seek help. What frightens her most is the fear that she will not be able to function normally as a shopowner and a woman who enjoys independence. She hopes that through therapy, she can regain some sense of control over her life and memories, learning better coping mechanisms to manage her fears and feelings of inadequacy. Overall, Lena's current state reflects a complex interplay between triggers, maladaptive strategies, memory issues, and negative appraisals, each reinforcing the other in a self-perpetuating cycle. The fear that she is going crazy and her belief in her own inadequacy are driving her to seek therapeutic support to break this cycle and reclaim her sense of control and well-being.
